K.M. JOSEPH, C.J. (Oral)
 In all these cases, there is delay of 2243 days
in filing the revision. In support of the petition for

3
condonation of delay, it is, inter alia, stated, originally, as
follows:
 The judgment of the Tribunal was rendered on
19.04.2011. It was received on 30.04.2011. The matter
was discussed at various levels of the Department and,
accordingly, for filing the C.T.R., permission was received
by the Department on 08.07.2011. All the papers were
sent to the Deputy Commissioner, Commercial Tax, High
Court and, on the same day, the files were allotted. After
getting the approval for filing the Revisions, all the papers
with regard to the filing Revisions were sent to the
Deputy Commissioner and, on the same day, the files
were allotted for preparing of the C.T.R. by the office of
the learned Chief Standing Counsel at Nainital to the
then Brief Holder Mr. Sudhir Kumar. He sought
translated copies. Though, it was difficult for the
Department to serve/available correct translation of the
orders of the Tribunal, therefore, some time was
consumed in translating the orders. That the translated
copy was received on 27.11.2014; but, due to over
burden in different cases, the State Counsel could not
draft the revisions. Subsequently, Mr. Sudhir Kumar,
who was earlier Brief Holder, his engagement was
withdrawn in the year 2013; but, the In-charge Officer
did not re-allot the files. The reasons are best known to
him. However, as and when the said fact came to the
knowledge of the Department, the files were re-allotted,
as there were several files pending for preparation of
C.T.R., which also consumed time. It is stated that,
against the erring official, notice was issued and charge-sheet was also issued. It is also stated as follows:

4
ì10. That after perusing the relevant
record and going through the proposal for
filing Commercial Tax Revision, the State
Counsel drafted the accompanying
Commercial Tax Revision, which is being
filed without any further delay.
11. That in the catena of judgments the
Honíble Supreme Court has held that in
the event of decision to file appeal needed
prompt action should be pursued by the
officer responsible to file the appeal and
he should be made personally responsible
for lapses, if any.î
2. Having gone through the affidavit and noticed
the manner in which the delay is sought to be explained,
particularly, without details of the dates also, we are
unable to accept the explanation given for condonation of
2243 daysí delay in filing these Revisions.
3. In such circumstances, the delay condonation
applications in all these cases will stand dismissed.
Consequently, the Commercial Tax Revisions will also
stand dismissed.
 (V.K. Bist, J.) (K.M. Joseph, C.J.)
23.11.2017 23.11.2017
